taxonomic_note: Legacy Master Plant Pool name Chamaesyce villifera is normalized to the current accepted Euphorbia name.
look_here_first: Low spreading sandmat distinguished by conspicuous soft hairs on stems and leaves.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local legacy Chamaesyce source; current Kew explicitly treats Chamaesyce villifera as a synonym of accepted Euphorbia villifera, native in Texas.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; broader exact-county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbiaceae/Euphorbia: milky latex and highly reduced flowers grouped into a cyathium; in sandmat spurges, opposite leaves, stem habit, hairiness, and capsule traits are especially useful.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: The name is the cue: villifera = hairy. In this set it is the obvious pubescent sandmat, unlike the nearly smooth E. serpens.
